newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades near 3.05/10 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades near 3.05/10 pct.

text.p: German call money traded slightly firmer between 3.05/10 percent at the start of the week with dealers predicting rates may nudge lower later as banks' reserve holdings had improved since Friday.

Call money rates on Friday had fallen back towards 3.05 percent after the Bundesbank injected 3.2 billion marks in emergency funds into the money market to pull rates off their peaks at 3.20 percent back towards three percent.
"The liquidity from the quick tender really helped," one trader said, adding "the reserve numbers now look better than they did before."
Dealers said the bulk of trades was conducted between 3.05/10 percent in mostly calm conditions.

After the Bundesbank on Friday injected additional funds, dealers were confident this week's weekly securities repurchase tender award would also be sufficient to help the market negotiate month-end without seeing great rate fluctuations.
"We expect to see a little bit more money injected this week and this should help us with month end," another dealer added.
Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum had said on Friday that German rates would remain steady in the near-term.
Banks' holdings in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank climbed to 45.6 billion marks on Friday from 42.4 billion held on Thursday.
Average month holdings stood at 40.9 billion marks on Sunday compared with 40.3 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings were steady at 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rates FIONA were set at 3.12767 percent on Monday compared with 3.12800 on Friday.
